In 2022, he was named in the [[NBL1 Central]] All-Star Five playing for the [[Southern Tigers]]. After a season of [[college basketball]] in the United States for [[UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball|UC Riverside]], he returned to the NBL1 Central in 2023 and helped the [[West Adelaide Bearcats]] win the [[List of NBL1 Central champions|championship]] while earning grand final MVP and All-Star Five honours. He joined the Illawarra Hawks for the [[2023–24 NBL season]] and then had a [[List of New Zealand NBL champions|championship]]-winning season with the [[Canterbury Rams]] in the [[2024 New Zealand NBL season]]. With the Rams, he was named [[New Zealand NBL Finals Most Valuable Player Award|grand final MVP]], [[New Zealand NBL Most Valuable Player Award|league MVP]] and [[New Zealand NBL All-Star Five|All-Star Five]]. ==Early life and career== Olbrich was born [[Adelaide]], [[South Australia]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/under-the-radar-olbrich-primed-for-monster-nbl24|title=Under the radar: Olbrich primed for monster NBL24|work=Hawks.com.au|date=11 August 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728052857/https://www.hawks.com.au/news/under-the-radar-olbrich-primed-for-monster-nbl24|archive-date=28 July 2024}} He grew up playing basketball with his older brother Mitchell and his father Greg.{{cite web|last=Egan|first=Brendon|url=https://www.thepress.co.nz/sport/350345616/canterbury-rams-australian-standout-lachlan-olbrich-thrives-through-adversity|title=Canterbury Rams' Australian standout Lachlan Olbrich thrives through adversity|work=[[The Press]]|date=20 July 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240729095610/https://www.thepress.co.nz/sport/350345616/canterbury-rams-australian-standout-lachlan-olbrich-thrives-through-adversity|archive-date=29 July 2024}} He attended [[Reynella East College]] in Adelaide, where he played basketball and [[volleyball]].{{cite web|url=https://gohighlanders.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/lachlan-olbrich/6807|title=Lachlan Olbrich|work=[[UC Riverside Highlanders]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728053738/https://gohighlanders.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/lachlan-olbrich/6807|archive-date=28 July 2024}} He represented South Australia at national basketball championships in 2020 and 2021. In 2021, Olbrich played one game for the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in the [[Waratah League]] and two games for the [[Southern Tigers]] in the [[NBL1 Central]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Lachlan-Olbrich/604789|title=Lachlan Olbrich|work=Australiabasket.com|access-date=28 July 2024|url-access=subscription}} In October 2021, Olbrich signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) as a development player for the [[2021–22 NBL season|2021–22 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/adelaide-36ers-sign-local-talent-olbrich-to-dp-contract|title=Adelaide 36ers sign local talent Olbrich to DP contract|work=Adelaide36ers.com.au|date=15 October 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728054643/https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/adelaide-36ers-sign-local-talent-olbrich-to-dp-contract|archive-date=28 July 2024}} He appeared in three games for the 36ers during the season. Olbrich re-joined the Southern Tigers of the NBL1 Central for the [[2022 NBL1 season|2022 season]]. He was named to the All-Star Five{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/nbl1central/photos/a.1198883153481900/5394815403888633/|title=Your 2022 NBL1 Central Men's All Star Five|work=facebook.com/nbl1central|date=14 August 2022|access-date=28 July 2024}} and won the Frank Angove Award as the league's best under 23 player.{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/nbl1central/photos/a.1198883153481900/5394817863888387/|title=Congratulations to Lachlan Olbrich on winning the 2022 NBL1 Central Frank Angove Award|work=facebook.com/nbl1central|date=14 August 2022|access-date=28 July 2024}} In 12 games, he averaged 19.8 points, 10.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 blocks per game. ==College career== Olbrich moved to the United States to play [[college basketball]] for the [[UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball|UC Riverside Highlanders]] of the [[Big West Conference]] in the [[2022–23 UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball team|2022–23 season]].{{cite web|last=Badkin|first=Liam|url=https://central.rookieme.com/basketball/olbrich-ostensibly-on-the-right-path/|title=Olbrich ostensibly on the right path|work=central.rookieme.com|date=29 November 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728055744/https://central.rookieme.com/basketball/olbrich-ostensibly-on-the-right-path/|archive-date=28 July 2024}} He averaged 11.4 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game. He was subsequently named Big West Freshman of the Year and earned All-Big West Honorable Mention honours. He became just the second Big West Freshman of the Year in UC Riverside history.{{cite web|url=https://bigwest.org/news/2023/3/6/the-big-west-unveils-2022-23-mens-basketball-all-conference-team-major-awards-and-specialty-awards.aspx|title=The Big West Unveils 2022-23 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team, Major Awards and Specialty Awards|work=[[Big West Conference]]|date=6 March 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728060411/https://bigwest.org/news/2023/3/6/the-big-west-unveils-2022-23-mens-basketball-all-conference-team-major-awards-and-specialty-awards.aspx|archive-date=28 July 2024}} ==Professional career== Olbrich returned to the NBL1 Central and joined the [[West Adelaide Bearcats]] for the [[2023 NBL1 season|2023 season]]. He was once again named to the All-Star Five and won his second Frank Angove Award.{{cite web|url=https://nbl1.com.au/article/2023-nbl1-awards-tracker|title=2023 NBL1 Awards Tracker|work=NBL1.com.au|date=11 August 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728060941/https://nbl1.com.au/article/2023-nbl1-awards-tracker|archive-date=28 July 2024}} He helped the Bearcats reach the NBL1 Central grand final, where they defeated the [[Forestville Eagles]] 106–95 to win the [[List of NBL1 Central champions|championship]] behind Olbrich's 24 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. He was subsequently named grand final MVP.{{cite web|last=Badkin|first=Liam|url=https://central.rookieme.com/basketball/olbrich-owns-big-stage-with-damaging-decider/|title=Olbrich owns big stage with damaging decider|work=central.rookieme.com|date=14 August 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728061216/https://central.rookieme.com/basketball/olbrich-owns-big-stage-with-damaging-decider/|archive-date=28 July 2024}} In 18 games, he averaged 21.1 points, 9.0 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game. On 4 April 2023, Olbrich signed a three-year deal with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the NBL.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/hawks-secure-aussie-college-talent|title=Hawks Secure Aussie College Talent|work=NBL.com.au|date=4 April 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728061601/https://nbl.com.au/news/hawks-secure-aussie-college-talent|archive-date=28 July 2024}} He had a breakout showing in the pre-season NBL Blitz but struggled early in the regular season. Upon coach [[Justin Tatum]] taking over midway through the season, Olbrich went on to prove himself as a capable back-up for captain [[Sam Froling]].{{cite web|last=Latifi|first=Agron|url=https://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/8542293/lachlan-olbrich-aims-for-redemption-against-new-zealand-breakers/|title='I can't wait to see the WEC packed': Olbrich ahead of Hawks v Breakers nailbiter|work=[[Illawarra Mercury]]|date=3 March 2024|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240728074059/https://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/8542293/lachlan-olbrich-aims-for-redemption-against-new-zealand-breakers/|archive-date=28 July 2024}} In 31 games in the [[2023–24 NBL season]], he averaged 3.8 points and 3.1 rebounds per game. Following his first NBL season, he had hopes of declaring for the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last=Bruce|first=Jasper|url=https://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/8535455/hawks-olbrich-poised-to-shoot-nba-shot-in-2025/|title=Hawks' Olbrich poised to shoot NBA shot in 2025|work=[[Illawarra Mercury]]|publisher=[[Australian Associated Press]]|date=26 February 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240827044218/https://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/8535455/hawks-olbrich-poised-to-shoot-nba-shot-in-2025/|archive-date=27 August 2024}} Olbrich joined the [[Canterbury Rams]] of the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]] (NZNBL) for the [[2024 New Zealand NBL season|2024 season]].{{cite web|url=https://canterburyrams.basketball/rams-land-star-australian-prospect-lachlan-olbrich/|title=Rams Land Star Australian Prospect Lachlan Olbrich|work=canterburyrams.basketball|date=24 January 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124045324/https://canterburyrams.basketball/rams-land-star-australian-prospect-lachlan-olbrich/|archive-date=24 January 2024}} On the day he debuted for the Rams on 27 March, he was informed that his father had died in South Australia.
